1.explanation:
1. We turn on VS Code’s “format on save” and set Prettier as the default formatter in .vscode/settings.json.  
2. We configure Prettier to use proseWrap: "preserve" (so it won’t reflow lines) and tabWidth: 4 (so that Markdown nested blocks get their standard 4-space indent).  
3. We author a Markdown list item and nest raw HTML by indenting it exactly four spaces.  
4. Every time you save, Prettier treats the HTML block as Markdown content and reapplies list-block indentation—adding another four spaces at each run.  
By saving the file multiple times, you reproduce the runaway indenting bug seen in the screenshots.
1.bug_scenario: When you have an ordered list in Markdown and nest a raw HTML block (in this case an HTML <table>) by indenting it four spaces under the list item, Prettier’s "format on save" will repeatedly increase that indent on every save. On first save, the table moves from 4 to 8 spaces; on the next save, to 12; and so on, until the HTML drifts far off the intended nesting level.
